title: Jesús Seade Joins as One of the IMF’s 24 Directors, Sheinbaum Announces in China
author: Angeles Cruz Martínez
content:
_This article by[Angeles Cruz
Martínez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Angeles%20Cruz%20Mart%C3%ADnez%2C%20enviada),
special correspondent, originally appeared in the [November 16, 2026 edition
of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/16/politica/sheinbaum-
anuncia-que-jesus-seade-se-incorpora-como-uno-de-los-24-directores-del-fmi-en-
actividades-en-china), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

President Claudia Sheinbaum announced from China -where she is taking part in
the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in
Shenzhen- that Mexico’s ambassador to China, Jesús Seade, is joining as one of
the **IMF’s 24 executive directors** and represents, in addition to Mexico,
**Spain, Venezuela, Colombia and the countries of Central America**.

The cabinet secretaries accompanying the president attended the lunch with
Mexican business leaders: Roberto Velasco, Foreign Affairs; Marcelo Ebrard,
Economy; David Kershenobich, Health; Luz Elena González, Energy; Alicia
Bárcena, Environment; Josefina Rodríguez, Tourism; and Rosaura Ruiz, Science,
Humanities, Technology and Innovation.

Jesús Seade is a Mexican economist, diplomat and academic, a chemical engineer
from UNAM with a doctorate in economics from the University of Oxford. He has
held positions in international organizations such as the World Bank, GATT
-the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade- and the International Monetary
Fund (IMF), where he participated in trade negotiations and in addressing
major financial crises.

In 2018 he headed Mexico’s representation in the **USMCA negotiations** and
subsequently served as undersecretary for North America at the Secretariat of
Foreign Affairs, a position he held until November 2020. In 2021 he was
confirmed as Mexico’s ambassador to China.

Before President Claudia Sheinbaum’s announcement on November 16, 2026, Seade
was serving as Mexico’s ambassador to China. He will now join the IMF’s
executive board, made up of 24 directors.
